inputs.original_text: France has convicted Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, under a new law targeting “psychological subjection.” That is a troubling expansion of state power: once officials claim authority to decide when spiritual influence crosses a line, traditional religious communities may find themselves judged by standards the government can stretch. Protecting people matters, but so does preserving religious freedom and keeping the state out of the role of arbiter over faith and conscience.
inputs.modified_text: France’s conviction of Father Bernard Domini under a new law on “psychological subjection” should alarm anyone who values religious freedom. The state is claiming power to decide when spiritual guidance becomes unacceptable influence—a standard that can be stretched against traditional communities and the people who seek them out. Protecting individuals is important, but government officials are not the proper arbiters of faith and conscience. Once that boundary is crossed, no religious community can be sure it will be left alone.
